Include the decision to start Ruben Tejada in the leadoff spot and the implications of Manuel's juggling of players like Francoeur, Pagan, and Bay. Passage: SAN FRANCISCO - At least manager Jerry Manuel didn't even bother to put Jose Reyes in Friday's lineup against the Giants. Still, the manager's efforts to make up for Reyes' absence resulted in a few other head-scratching decisions.
At the very top of that list - literally - was batting Ruben Tejada, the 20-year-old rookie shortstop, in the leadoff spot followed by Jason Bay, not exactly a prototypical No. 2 hitter.
Manuel's strange tinkering with the lineup was primarily due to Reyes' lingering oblique injury. But it also was affected by his pledge to use Jeff Francoeur against lefthanded starters, and Barry Zito was on the mound Friday for the Giants.
Perhaps a more conventional approach with regular leadoff hitter Reyes on the shelf would be to start Angel Pagan, the next best option. But now that Carlos Beltran has been re-installed as the Mets' everyday centerfielder, Manuel insists that he will split time between Pagan and Francoeur, and Friday was Francoeur's turn.
"Well, I've got to make sure Francoeur gets some at-bats," Manuel said. "I think that Angel understands that for the most part. I think it is a little tough right now to get that lineup exactly like you want it with trying to juggle different things here. I had told [Francoeur] that he was going to play and I feel pretty good about him being in there tonight."
The Mets were a little more optimistic Friday about Reyes after he took batting practice from the left side, which had been the biggest issue for him. Reyes looked tentative taking those swings, and just the fact that he was doing it was incongruous with what the Mets were saying about their shortstop only 24 hours earlier.
After Reyes was scratched from Thursday's game, he said he was banned from any activity until the pain in his right side had disappeared. But when asked Friday how he was feeling, Reyes replied, "About the same." Yet he was allowed to hit both indoors and later with his teammates on the field. Why the switch in plans? Apparently the prognosis had changed.
"I think what they wanted him to do was do an activity today of some sort," Manuel said. "Just one activity, and the activity that he wanted to do was swing. He could have taken grounds balls and threw, but he wanted to swing. That was the thing that would determine where he was and what he could do. I think he felt pretty good after that."
Pressed on a possible return date, Manuel suggested Sunday at the earliest, a game that would allow Reyes to bat from the right side against the Giants' Jonathan Sanchez. Of course, that depends on how Reyes feels Saturday after taking batting practice, and he's defied just about every prediction to this point.
"If the thing is barking or whatever," Manuel said, "then I think they'll just back him off."
The Mets did give themselves some infield flexibility by calling up Justin Turner from Triple-A Buffalo and optioning Nick Evans. On Thursday, the team's emergency shortstop was David Wright if anything happened to either Tejada or Alex Cora.
By sitting Pagan, the manager chose to use Tejada and his .299 on-base percentage in the leadoff spot. For Bay, it was his first turn in the second spot since Oct. 3 of last season with the Red Sox. But he was less concerned about his place in the order as compared to his need to produce at the plate.

At the end of the year, I might not have the big numbers I had in the past, but that's not my No. 1 goal right now. Now it really is a day-to-day thing. To go out there every day and try to do something to help the team win."

Problem Set 1 [Benchmarking: inter - organizational comparisons] The Problem Sets 1 and 2 are based on the article
Grifell-Tatjé, E. and C.A.K Lovell (1996), “Deregulation and Productivity Decline: The Case of the Spanish Savings Banks,” European Economic Review 40, 1281-1303.
Motivation
The data in the Excel file is a real one and belongs to the Spanish savings banks in the period 1986 - 1991. Spain signed the accession to the European Union (EU) in June 1985 and it was effective since 1986. Therefore, we are analyzing the banking sector in the first years after Spain's entry into the EU. For the entry, the EU required the liberation of the financial sector, which had traditionally been heavily regulated. This requirement particularly affected the Spanish savings banks which were not allowed to offer their services outside their own geographical region. Savings banks concentrated on retail banking, providing checking, savings and loan services to individuals. They did little commercial business, and they conducted very few foreign exchange transactions, these activities being heavily concentrated in the private banking sector. By 1987, however, all interest rates and service charges were freed, and in 1989 savings banks finally were allowed to branch outside their geographic region. Additionally, investment requirements were gradually phased out during l989-1992. The l986-1991 period can be characterized as one in which the rules of the game changed quite dramatically in the Spanish banking sector. While a constantly changing environment caused operating problems for savings bank managements, it also created opportunities for growth. Particularly since 1989 two features have dominated the savings bank segment of the industry: rapid branching, much of it interregional, and consolidation through mergers and acquisitions.
Purpose
The main objective of this problem set, and the following one, is to analyze the impact on savings banks of Spain’s entry into the EU. To do this, these problem sets apply techniques of benchmark. The Problem Set 1 is based on inter - organizational comparisons and the Problem Set 2 on longitudinal – dynamic comparison. This problem set 1 asks about technical efficiency, super-efficiency and layers classification of savings banks. Problem set 2 reproduces the main aspects of the article “Deregulation and Productivity Decline: The Case of the Spanish Savings Banks,” which are based on longitudinal benchmark.
The variables: Outputs and Inputs
In the banking literature there is a lack of agreement in defining what a bank produces. A possibility is the value added approach. In this approach deposits are included among the outputs because they produce a very important share of bank value added. The outputs and inputs have been defined following this approach. The main reason for this preference is that input consumption has a closer relationship with the number of loans and deposits than with their value. We have adopted this point of view, but we do not have enough information to define all the inputs in terms of their quantities. Therefore, for two inputs we use their value. In these cases, these values must be deflated to a base period.
 
The data set defines three outputs and three inputs. The three basic outputs are: the number of loan accounts (OUT1), the number of checking accounts (OUT2), and the number of savings accounts (OUT3). We have defined three inputs: the number of employees (INP1), expenditure on materials (INP2), and direct expenditure on buildings plus accounting depreciation (INP3). The expenditures on materials and buildings have been deflated to 1986 prices, using the consumer price index.
As a direct consequence of the mergers and acquisitions, the number of savings banks in operation decreased sharply during this period, from 77 in 1986 to 56 in 1991. Some of these mergers involved more than two savings banks. Over the entire period there have occurred 15 mergers and acquisitions, 14 of them taking place in the years 1990 and 1991. The sample is the population in the years 1986, 1989 and 1991 and almost it in the years 1987 (76 out of 77), 1988 (75 out of 77) and 1990 (59 out of 64).
Questions:
Note: Questions are based on the assumption of a technology with constant returns to scale and output oriented technical efficiency.
1.- Calculate the output-oriented technical efficiency of these years (from 1986 to 1991) assuming constant returns to scale (CRS) and defining a contemporaneous technology, which the article calls “adjacent periods”.
2.- Identify the observations that are output-oriented technically efficient. List them. Is it possible to identify a group of always efficient savings banks?
3.- Reproduce the Table 3, on page 1292, of the article “Deregulation and Productivity Decline: The Case of the Spanish Savings Banks.”
4.- Rank the efficient savings banks from the best to the worst efficient for the years from 1986 to 1991. Is this ranking stable over time? Is it possible to identify one (or more) excellent savings bank(s) based on this super-efficiency ranking?
5.- We can also make a classification of the savings banks based on layers. How many layers can we define for each of the years? Is the number of layers the same?
6.- Now, pay attention to the observations. Are they in the same layer over time? Are they jumping? or Are they jumping erratically? Can we identify a pattern in any of them (ascending, descending, stable,..,)?

The annotation is a small review of the work and its author. Here you can write a short summary of the content and usefulness of the work. Write whether the work has any limitations, and include a description of what readers it is intended for. A Chicago annotated bibliography should be presented in alphabetical order by the last name of the author.
If you write an annotated bibliography, it can help you kick-start research for your paper. Also, it will demonstrate that you understand research in your sphere of study. An annotated Chicago style bibliography will inform readers of the accuracy, relevance and the quality of sources that you have used.
Many students think that annotations, summaries, and abstracts are the same things. A summary is a brief work retelling. It doesn’t involve an interpretive work statement. An annotation is a work interpretation in relation to your own research. Sometimes you may include some criticisms about the course that you use.
The purpose of an annotated bibliography will determine the length of the annotation. Reflect on the source after assessing and summarizing. If you want to have a broad picture of what was said about your topic, use different sources. Investigate how scholarly sources treat your topic differently than popular sources. However, you should avoid newspapers, or popular sites if you need to use only scholarly sources in your paper.
Why should you pay attention to what an author says?
For whom are the sources intended?
What is the focus of the source?
What research methods the author used?
What is the thesis statement of the author?
Use the library catalog to search for journal articles, books, and other documents that may involve ideas and information on your topic. Review all citations that you include in your paper. Select only works that present perspectives on your subject. Choose the annotated bibliography Chicago style and have RefWorks prepare the bibliography.
You don’t need to read the entire work to write an effective annotation. If you use a book, read the introduction and the conclusion. Also, read notes provided by the author. You should read the author’s credentials about the work. Check out the sources that the author uses to write a conclusion.
Annotations can be descriptive, summarizing qualifications of the author, research methods, and arguments. The quality of scholarship in an article or book can be evaluated in the annotation. Consider the quality of the evidence and the logic of the author’s arguments. Also, you may explain why the sources are relevant.
Once you have read and gathered plenty of sources, it is important to cite them in an appropriate Chicago style annotated bibliography format. The reason for citing is to give credit to authors whose thoughts and ideas you have used in your paper. Even if you don’t include a direct quote, you have to give credit to authors whose ideas contributed to your work.
If you cite sources properly, it will help your readers to find sources easily. You will be accused of plagiarism if you don’t cite sources upon which you did your research. If you use and present other ideas as your own, you plagiarize. Even if you rephrase some author without including a citation, you plagiarize. In this case, you can be punished with a failing grade or even expulsion from your institution.
Every entry in a bibliography should contain information commonly included in works cited list. If you cite a book, you should include a title, an author, publication place, and publication year. The format for your citation should be specified by your professor. The annotation follows the bibliographic information and it describes the source’s contents.
Ask your professor if you have any questions about how you should compose your annotation. Look at other annotated bibliographies as examples. Many books include them. Also, you can use the Internet, as there are a lot of examples you can use. It is important to look through such examples if you want to get a high grade.
When you include every source in your annotated bibliography, write a short descriptive paragraph consisting of four to five sentences which can involve relevance to your topic as well. Present a clear indication of every source relevancy, quality, and accuracy. To write a good annotated bibliography, read the instructions carefully.
You should be clear about the type of annotated bibliography that you need to write. Provide a clear overview of the arguments, evidence, and conclusions in the descriptive part. Analyze the content, and comment on the arguments’ strengths and weaknesses. Write why the source is useful for your research topic.

“Yes. But there's a better approach. To know you're going to die, and to be prepared for it at any time. That's better. That way you can actually be more involved in your life while you're living.”

Am I being the person I want to be?'” He turned his head to his shoulder as if the bird were there now. “Is today the day I die?” he said. Morrie borrowed freely from all religions. He was born Jewish, but became an agnostic when he was a teenager, partly because of all that had happened to him as a child. He enjoyed some of the philosophies of Buddhism and Christianity, and he still felt at home, culturally, in Judaism. He was a religious mutt, which made him even more open to the students he taught over the years. And the things he was saying in his final months on earth seemed to transcend all religious differences. Death has a way of doing that. “The truth is, Mitch,” he said, “once you learn how to die, you learn how to live.” I nodded. “I'm going to say it again,” he said. “Once you learn how to die, you learn how to live.” He smiled, and I realized what he was doing. He was making sure I absorbed this point, without embarrassing me by asking. It was part of what made him a good teacher. Did you think much about death before you got sick, I asked.

(In the school literature clubroom…)

Monika: “Alright, that concludes today’s meeting! MC, Sayori, Natsuki, Yuri, you all had some great poems.”

MC: “Thanks, Monika! I really enjoyed listening to everyone’s poems today.”

Sayori: “Yeah, they were all so different but equally amazing. It’s always so inspiring to hear what you all come up with.”

Natsuki: “Well, I definitely liked some more than others, but variety is a good thing, I guess.”

Yuri: “I must say, your poem really caught my attention, MC. The imagery was quite vivid, and you captured emotions perfectly.”

Monika: “Oh, MC, I have to agree with Yuri. Your poem had such depth and beauty to it. I could tell you put a lot of thought into it.”

MC: “Thank you, guys. I’m really happy you liked it. Sayori, your poem was really uplifting and had such a positive message.”

Sayori: “Aww, thanks, MC. I tried to write something happy and motivational this time.”

Natsuki: “Well, I thought your poem was a bit too fluffy for my taste, Sayori. But hey, if it made you happy, that’s what matters.”

Yuri: “Natsuki, I loved your poem as well. It had a simplicity to it that made it quite charming.”

Natsuki: “Uh, thanks, Yuri. I didn’t think you would enjoy it that much, considering our different writing styles.”

Monika: “That’s the beauty of our literature club, Natsuki. We’re all so different, yet our unique perspectives bring something special to the table.”

MC: “Exactly. It’s fascinating to see how our individual writing styles reflect our personalities.”

Sayori: “Yeah, it’s like a little glimpse into each other’s minds and hearts. I love being a part of this club.”

Yuri: “I agree. The literature club is a safe space where we can express ourselves freely through our writing.”

Monika: “And I’m so proud to see how far we’ve come as a club. We’ve grown both individually and as a team. Anyways, can’t wait to see you tomorrow!”

MC: “Yeah, me too! Same time, same place?”

Monika: “Of course! See you all then!”

(As the members start leaving the clubroom, they can’t help but feel a sense of accomplishment and unity. Each of them cherishes the friendships they’ve formed and the support they’ve received through their writing journey. Just then, Monika notices a student leaning against the wall & caressing her belly - and she is very clearly in the 7th month of pregnancy.)

Monika: “Excuse me, are you alright? You seem to be in some discomfort.”

Pregnant Student: “Oh, I’m fine. Just taking a little break, my feet are killing me.”

Monika: “Would you like a seat? We have some extra chairs in the clubroom.”

Pregnant Student: “Oh, that would be wonderful, thank you.”

(The pregnant student enters the clubroom and takes a seat, while the other members gather around to see if she needs any assistance - and the size of her baby bump makes it obvious that she’s having twins.)

MC: “Wow, twins! That’s amazing!”

Sayori: “Congratulations! That’s such exciting news. How are you feeling?”

Pregnant Student: “Thank you! I’m feeling a bit tired lately, but overall I’m doing well. Just trying to take it easy and prepare for their arrival. Baby A is constantly doing somersaults. (Noticing the various poetry books in the clubroom) I see you are all poetry enthusiasts.”

Monika: “Hold up…where could Natsuki be?”

Sayori: “You’re right, Monika. This isn’t like her at all. Yuri, could you try calling her?”

Yuri: (rubbing her 7-month baby bump) “Certainly, I’ll give it a try.”

(Yuri pulls out her phone and dials Natsuki’s number. The room echoes with the sound of ringing.)

Yuri: (anxiously) “No answer. She might just be delayed.”

Monika: (concerned) “I hope that's all it is. Natsuki is typically very punctual.”

Sayori: “Is it possible she forgot about the meeting?”

Yuri: (pondering) “That’s quite improbable. We’ve been preparing for this for weeks.” (placing a hand on her baby bump) “Ow…”

Monika: “Yuri, are you okay?”

Yuri: (wincing) “It’s just a slight cramp. Don’t worry.”

Monika: “Are you sure? Maybe sitting down would help.”

Yuri: (nodding) “Yes, that’d be wise. Sayori, can you keep trying to reach Natsuki? We’ll be here for Yuri.”

Sayori: “Absolutely, Yuri. Take it easy.”

(Yuri slowly takes a seat, gently rubbing her baby bump. Monika joins her, offering a comforting hand.)

Monika: “Yuri, you’ve been overworking lately. You should relax.”

Yuri: (sighing) “I know, but I want everything to be perfect for our upcoming event. I can't help but worry about Natsuki.”

Monika: “Your health and the baby’s are the priority now. We’ll manage the club activities today.”

Yuri: (reluctantly) “You’re right. I’ll try to relax. Thank you for your concern.”

(Meanwhile, Sayori continues to call Natsuki, but it goes straight to voicemail.)

Sayori: (worried) “Her phone is still off. I hope nothing’s wrong.”

Monika: “Maybe we should visit her house after the meeting?”

Sayori: “Great idea, Monika. We shouldn’t leave things uncertain.”

Yuri: (attempting to stand) “Agreed. Let’s wrap up quickly, and then head over there.” (feeling another stronger cramp) “Ah…!”

Monika: “Yuri, that seemed more intense. Are you really okay?”

Yuri: (clenching her teeth) “I’m okay. Just some discomfort. Let’s hurry.”

Sayori: “Yuri, this doesn’t seem normal. Should we call a doctor?”

Yuri: (panting) “No…I’m fine. We can’t abandon Natsuki if she needs us.”

Monika: “Yuri, the baby’s wellbeing is just as critical.”

Yuri: (tears forming) “I know…but we can’t leave Natsuki. Let’s just check on her first.”

Sayori: (concerned) “Alright, but promise you’ll let us help if things worsen.”

Yuri: (smiling weakly) “I promise, Sayori.”

(They gather their belongings and head to Natsuki’s house, their worries mounting.)

(At Natsuki’s house, they ring the doorbell repeatedly. No response.)

Monika: “Natsuki, are you home? It’s us—Monika, Yuri, and Sayori!”

Sayori: “Do we try knocking louder?”

Yuri: (holding her abdomen) “Let’s hope she’s okay… Oh, this pain is unbearable…”

Monika: “Yuri, we need to get you to a hospital. You’re in serious pain.”

Yuri: (tearfully) “I can’t leave Natsuki…I need to know she’s safe… Please, just a bit longer…”

(Natsuki suddenly opens the door, shocked by Yuri’s condition.)

Natsuki: “Yuri?! What’s happening? Are you alright?”

Yuri: (struggling with pain) “I…just wanted to…make sure you’re okay…”

Natsuki: “Worried about me? Why?”

Monika: “Yuri has been in severe pain, but she wanted to check on you first.”

##New Prompt##

The Annual Innovative Robotics Competition (AIRC) has concluded with m teams participating. The rankings are available: the team in the j-th place constructed r_j robots. The teams are ranked based on the number of robots constructed, so r_1 ≥ r_2 ≥ ... ≥ r_m.

Your task is to help the organizers allocate gold, silver, and bronze trophies. Let the counts of these trophies be g_k, s_k, and b_k, respectively. The following conditions must be met for the allocation:

  * Each of the three types of trophies must be awarded at least once (i.e., g_k > 0, s_k > 0, b_k > 0);
  * The number of gold trophies must be strictly less than the number of silver trophies and the number of bronze trophies (i.e., g_k < s_k and g_k < b_k, but there are no constraints between s_k and b_k);
  * Each gold-winning team must construct strictly more robots than any silver-winning team;
  * Each silver-winning team must construct strictly more robots than any bronze-winning team;
  * Each bronze-winning team must construct strictly more robots than any team that doesn't win a trophy;
  * The total number of awarded teams (g_k + s_k + b_k) should not exceed half the number of participating teams (for instance, if m=30, the maximum number of teams that can be awarded is 15, and if m=50, then the maximum is 25).

The organizers wish to maximize the total number of teams receiving trophies (i.e., to maximize g_k + s_k + b_k) while meeting the above constraints. Find the optimal way to allocate the trophies.

Input

The first line of the input contains an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 10000) — the number of test cases.

Each test case starts with an integer m (1 ≤ m ≤ 4⋅10^5) — the number of AIRC teams. The second line of each test case contains integers r_1, r_2, ..., r_m (0 ≤ r_j ≤ 10^6), where r_j is the number of robots constructed by the team at the j-th position. These values r_j are sorted in non-increasing order, i.e., r_1 ≥ r_2 ≥ ... ≥ r_m.

The sum of m over all test cases does not exceed 4⋅10^5.

Output

Print t lines, where the j-th line contains the answer to the j-th test case.

The answer should consist of three non-negative integers g_k, s_k, b_k.

  * Print g_k=s_k=b_k=0 if it is impossible to distribute the trophies while satisfying all conditions.
  * Otherwise, print three positive integers g_k, s_k, b_k — the possible counts of gold, silver, and bronze trophies, respectively. The sum of g_k + s_k + b_k should be the maximum possible. If there are multiple valid answers, print any of them.

Example

Input
```
4
15
6 5 5 4 3 3 3 2 2 2 1 1 1 1 1
5
10 8 5 3 1
1
1000000
25
50 45 45 40 35 33 33 30 25 20 19 18 17 15 14 14 14 14 13 12 11 11 11 11 10
```

Output
```
1 2 5
0 0 0
0 0 0
2 4 7
```

Note

In the first test case, it is possible to allocate 1 gold, 2 silver, and 5 bronze trophies. The team that constructed 6 robots receives a gold trophy, teams that constructed 5 robots receive silver trophies, and teams that constructed 3 and 4 robots receive bronze trophies. All conditions are met and it maximizes the number of awarded teams. Other valid distributions such as 1, 3, 4 also exist.

In the second and third test cases, it is impossible to distribute the trophies as there aren't enough participants to meet the conditions.

As Jeff and Annie settled into the cozy comfort of their living room, the day’s exhaustion became apparent on Annie’s face. A sigh escaped her lips as she sunk into the plush couch, rubbing her temples with gentle movements. She glanced at Jeff, the corners of her mouth turning upward in a hopeful smile.

“Hey, Jeff,” she began, her voice carrying a faint trace of weariness. “Do you think… do you think you could, umm, maybe lick my feet for the evening? It might help me relax.”

Her request caught Jeff off guard, his eyebrows raising in surprise. Thoughts raced through his mind as he considered Annie’s proposition, realizing it was something they had never done before. In a brief moment of hesitation, Jeff’s reluctant agreement made its way to his lips. He decided to give it a try, vowing to keep his reservations quiet.

“Sure, Annie. I mean, if that’s what you need to unwind, I can give it a shot,” Jeff responded, his tone laced with curiosity. He watched as Annie’s face lit up with a mix of gratitude and anticipation, her energy sparks manifesting in her eyes.

Annie carefully lifted one foot, her delicate toes peeking out from beneath the weight of the day’s wear and tear. Jeff took a deep breath, trying to steady the building mixture of reluctance and excitement within him. He leaned forward, his fingers wrapping around Annie’s ankle as he positioned himself on the floor in front of her. The smoothness of her skin sent an unexpected shiver down his spine.

Jeff brought his face closer, his warm breath lightly teasing Annie’s foot. He hesitated for a moment, searching for the right approach. With a touch of tenderness, he brushed his lips against her arch, feeling a soft sigh escape Annie’s mouth. A tangible connection blossomed between them as Jeff’s playful tongue grazed the sole of her foot, tracing the lines and curves with delicate precision.

Surprisingly, Jeff found himself sinking deeper into the moment. The worries and skepticism that had initially clouded his mind continued to dissipate as he focused solely on providing Annie with relaxation and pleasure. His own reservations and judgments faded into the background as he discovered an unanticipated enjoyment in this unique experience.

With each leisurely lick, Jeff reveled in the sensation of Annie’s skin beneath his tongue. The saltiness of her day mingled with the delicate sweetness that was purely Annie, creating a unique flavor that awakened his senses. His earlier reluctance rapidly transformed into an eagerness to make her feel cherished, adored.

Jeff’s actions were meticulous and measured, taking care not to miss a single inch of Annie’s feet. He firmly believed that if he was going to commit to this, he would do it wholeheartedly. His tongue traced patterns across the tops of her toes, exploring the crevices and recesses with a perfect balance of tenderness and fervor.

In the midst of their silent communion, Jeff noticed Annie’s body relaxing more and more. The tension of the day melted away, replaced by a peaceful tranquility that radiated from her core. He could feel her gentle sighs of contentment reverberate through the vibrations between them, proof that his newfound willingness had provided the solace she had needed.

Time seemed to lose its relevance as Jeff continued his ministrations, each lick a testament to his commitment. The room fell into a comfortable hush, enveloping the couple in its intimate embrace. Jeff couldn’t help but smile, his heart swelling with a newfound appreciation for Annie’s vulnerability, their connection, and the beauty that lay within the unexpected.

As Jeff finally concluded his sweet exploration, he couldn’t help but lift his gaze to meet Annie’s eyes. The tenderness in her expression mirrored the affection that now swelled within him. They shared a moment, both deeply moved by the unspoken understanding that had blossomed from an unconventional request.

Annie’s voice, gentle and filled with gratitude, broke the stillness. “Thank you, Jeff. That was exactly what I needed.”

Jeff merely nodded, feeling a lump forming in his throat, at a loss for words. He realized that sometimes in life, we stumble upon unexpected moments of authenticity, surprising ourselves with new depths of love and understanding. (In the lively yet serene environment of the school literature clubroom…)

Monika: “…where is everyone? MC mentioned his arrival eventually, and both Natsuki & Yuri promised they’d bring their poetic compositions for today.”

Sayori: “I’m not exactly sure. Perhaps they got caught up with unforeseen matters. But hey, why don't we use this opportunity to brainstorm our upcoming agenda for the club in the meantime?”

Monika: “That sounds like a great plan. Sayori, do you have any innovative ideas for club activities we can engage in this month?”

Sayori: “I was contemplating organizing a poetry slam competition! Each member could craft a poem, then perform it before the club. It would be an engaging way to display our creativity and literary talent.”

Monika: “That’s an excellent suggestion, Sayori! I appreciate the idea of encouraging everyone to share their work enthusiastically. Let’s definitely pursue this!”

(Natsuki and Yuri then walk into the clubroom carrying their poems. Natsuki, who is seven months pregnant, moves cautiously.)

Natsuki: “Apologies for our tardiness, everyone. I nearly closed the car door on Yuri’s foot. Pregnancy brain seems to be affecting me in full force.”

Yuri: “It’s alright, Natsuki. I’m just pleased that we arrived on time. I’m eager to share our poetic compositions with everyone.”

Monika: “Perfect timing! We just started discussing our next club activity. Sayori proposed a poetry slam competition, and I think it’s a wonderful idea. What’s your opinion on this?”

Natsuki: “That sounds enjoyable! I’m up for it. A friendly competition might help distract me from the approaching childbirth. By the way, the baby has been quite active lately, kicking a lot. It’s both thrilling and slightly overwhelming.”

Yuri: “I concur, Natsuki. A poetry slam competition would be a fantastic platform to exhibit our talents and foster camaraderie. I’m eager to hear everyone’s creations.”

Sayori: “Hooray! I’m delighted everyone is enthusiastic about it. Let’s start planning the specifics to ensure the event’s success. I’ll make sure to prepare some snacks to keep our energy up during the event.”

Monika: “Great! Let’s schedule a date for the competition and begin promoting it to the broader school community. I have a feeling this will be a significant and memorable event for all of us.”

(The literature club members excitedly start planning the poetry slam competition, eager to share their creativity with each other and the rest of the school. However, on the day of the poetry slam competition, an unexpected situation arises—Natsuki’s water breaks, signaling that she is going into labor.)

Natsuki: “Oh no, why now? Why does this have to happen on the day of our competition?!”

Yuri: “Someone, quickly! Call an ambulance-”

Natsuki: “Yuri, I doubt they’ll arrive in time…it’s happening too rapidly…”

Monika: “Don’t worry, Natsuki. We’re here to support you. Sayori, ensure the ambulance is on its way. Yuri, stay with Natsuki and help keep her calm. We’ll handle this together.”

(Sayori rushes to call for help, while Yuri remains by Natsuki’s side, comforting her. Monika directs the remaining club members to set up a makeshift birthing area in the clubroom.)

Natsuki: “This is unbelievable. I’m really frightened, guys…”

Monika: “You’re not alone, Natsuki. We’re all here for you. Focus on your breathing and trust that we’ll support you and the baby.”

(Yuri stays by Natsuki’s side, holding her hand and offering words of encouragement as they await the ambulance’s arrival. The rest of the club members do their best to make Natsuki comfortable and support her through the unexpected labor. Suddenly, Sayori gasps in shock.)

Sayori: “Natsuki, I think I can see the baby’s head! The baby is arriving now!”

Natsuki: “Oh gosh, I can feel it too! It’s happening, it’s really happening…”

Monika: “Remain calm, Natsuki. We’re all here with you. Just keep breathing and push when you feel ready.”

(Yuri and the other club members gather around Natsuki, offering words of encouragement and support as she goes through labor in the clubroom.)

Sayori: “The head is almost out, Natsuki. Keep pushing and breathing; we're all here for you…”

Sayori: “Oh dear…what’s troubling you, my darling little boy? Are you feeling hungry?”

(She tenderly picks up her son and makes her way to the nursery. Once there, she prepares to nurse him.)

Sayori: “It’s all right, my little prince. Mama’s milk will help you flourish.”

(Sayori gently cradles her son in her arms, calming him as she settles into the nursery. She adjusts herself on the rocking chair and starts breastfeeding. He eagerly latches on, finding solace and sustenance in his mother’s milk.)

Sayori: (softly whispering) “There, there, my precious one. Mama’s here for you. You’re safe and cherished.”

(As her son continues to nurse, Sayori strokes his silky hair and hums a tender lullaby. She watches him closely, overwhelmed with a profound sense of maternal affection and protectiveness.)

Sayori: “You know, my little prince, Mama’s milk is more than just nourishment for your tummy. It’s brimming with warmth, immunoglobulins, and the essential nutrients you need to thrive and grow stronger. It’s our unique connection, a bond that no one else can replicate.”

(Sayori’s gaze shifts to her daughter, who’s peacefully slumbering in her nearby crib. She smiles, feeling deeply blessed to have her two precious children.)

Sayori: “I’m incredibly grateful to have both of you in my life. Being a mother is the most rewarding and enriching role I could ever dream of. I promise always to be here for you, in every joy and sorrow, providing boundless love and care you’ll ever need.”

(Sayori gently burps her son once he finishes nursing, lovingly patting his back. She then cradles him against her chest, rocking him tenderly.)

Sayori: “Shhh, my dear little boy. Mama’s arms will forever be your sanctuary. Whenever you seek comfort, know that I’ll be right here, loving and safeguarding you with all my heart.”

(Sayori continues to rock her son, treasuring the invaluable moments of motherhood. The room brims with warmth and love, as a new day dawns with infinite possibilities for their journey together.)

Sayori: “I vividly remember the day I invited my friends to feel you and your sister kick for the first time—back when I was four months pregnant, and my friends were blissfully unaware of my pregnancy. We were in the clubroom when you two first started kicking.”

The Ultimate Test

Crossover between Doctor Who, Magnum P.I (2018) and CSI: Crime Scene Investigation

The story revolves around a self-called "Parallel Doctor" with unknown objectives. His actions create a series of time fractures that the 14th Doctor must fix, all while protecting Rose. NOTE: This episode continues from The Ultimate Test, marking the first activation of Emergency Program One since The Parting of the Ways.

The Return

Martha Jones rejoins the Doctor's team, but the Daleks have returned. The Doctor, Rose, and Martha must stop them before their sinister plans come to fruition.

Out For Blood

Zombies begin to ravage the streets of Glasgow. Can the Doctor stop them in time?

Zombie Survival Tip 1

As the Doctor, Rose, and Martha attempt to stop the zombies, the Doctor has to dance again (callback to The Lost Child/The Doctor Dances). NOTE: This episode follows on from Out For Blood.

The Return of the Weeping Angels

The Weeping Angels return. Can the Doctor stop them in time?

Fragments of Forever

The TARDIS materializes on a future Earth where time has shattered into fragments. People from different eras coexist and struggle with temporal displacement issues. The Doctor discovers that the Chronosian is using this temporal instability to create an army of time-duplicates. Rose and Martha help unite a divided society, preventing a civil war, while the Doctor confronts the Chronosian.

The Forgotten Prophecy

The Doctor receives an enigmatic message from a psychic empath, indicating a prophecy that foretells the Chronosian’s ultimate plan for universal domination. Together, the Doctor and his companions decipher ancient hieroglyphics and uncover hidden temples on Gallifrey, learning that a lost Time Lord artifact, the Time Dynasticon, holds the key to restoring balance in time.

The Shifting Sands

The Doctor, Rose, and Martha journey back to Ancient Egypt where the Chronosian is utilizing Cleopatra’s tomb's mystical powers to manipulate time. The trio teams up with Cleopatra to outsmart the Chronosian and retrieve the Time Dynasticon. They face mummified monsters and treacherous sandstorms, battling to save history from being rewritten entirely.

Temporal Nexus

Arriving on a seemingly abandoned space station, the Doctor uncovers a web of temporal anomalies caused by the Chronosian’s experiments. Trapped in parallel timelines, Rose and Martha are forced to confront their deepest fears. The Doctor races against time to save his companions and close the temporal rift before it engulfs the entire station.

Reflections in Time

The TARDIS crash-lands on a parallel Earth where every person has a mirror duplicate. Chronosian exploits these duplicates to drain unsuspecting victims' life-force. The Doctor, Rose, and Martha navigate a world of doppelgängers, rescuing the innocent before the Chronosian’s dark plans can succeed.

The Return of John Smith

The Doctor seeks a way to bring back John Smith while maintaining his identity as the Doctor. He decides to clone himself and use the Chameleon Arch to create John Smith, presenting him to Joan (callback to Human Nature/The Family of Blood). He reminisces about honorary companion Rosa from Uncovered Time, wondering how she is doing.

The Final Countdown

The Doctor, Rose, and Martha discover the Chronosian’s secret stronghold within a pocket dimension. Inside, they encounter monstrous temporal guardians and traps that test their courage. As they confront the Chronosian, a long-forgotten ally of the Doctor arrives to help. The universe's fate hangs in the balance as the ultimate battle begins.

Season Finale: Clash of Time

The Doctor faces his most challenging battle yet as he teams up with his Parallel self, and the 9th and 11th versions, to defeat the Chronosian and save the universe. The Chronosian’s power has grown exponentially, and their plan to unravel time itself is near completion.

In a race against the clock, the Doctors navigate various periods and confront their personal demons. Parallel Doctor’s true intentions are revealed as he holds the key to stopping the Chronosian’s chaos. With his knowledge of the Time Dynasticon and temporal energy, he becomes a crucial asset in this epic battle.

As the Doctors and their companions unite, they face formidable challenges, including Weeping Angels, temporal traps, and distorted versions of themselves. The fate of all existence rests on their shoulders, with every decision bearing far-reaching consequences.

Throughout the struggle, the Doctors confront their vulnerabilities, learning the true meaning of sacrifice. Friendships are tested, loyalties questioned, and the very fabric of time hangs in the balance.

In a heart-stopping climax, the Doctor, with the help of his Parallel self, the 9th and 11th versions, devises a plan to trap the Chronosian in a time loop, preventing further chaos. With their combined wisdom and courage, they succeed in sealing the Chronosian, restoring the universe’s order.

Magnum and Horatio Caine join forces in the fight against the Chronosian, with KikoRiki characters providing comic relief during action scenes.

After the battle, the Doctor bids a bittersweet farewell to his Parallel self, acknowledging sacrifices made and knowledge gained from their shared experiences. He returns Martha to her timeline, thanking her for her bravery and loyalty.

The Doctor, with his bond with Rose stronger than ever, shares a quiet moment, knowing that their adventures are far from over. They step back into the TARDIS, ready for new journeys through time and space.

As the TARDIS dematerializes, the Doctor reflects on friendship’s power, the courage to face the unknown, and the enduring belief that hope prevails. And so, the Doctor’s adventures continue, a beacon of light in the vast darkness of the universe.

Note: This series incorporates elements from Doctor Who, Magnum P.I (2018), CSI: Crime Scene Investigation, Prison Break, and Kikoriki, creating an epic crossover combining sci-fi, mystery, comedy, and adventure genres. Each episode builds upon previous events, leading to a thrilling season finale where the universe's fate is at stake. While the Doctor (9th, 14th, 11th, and Parallel), Horatio, Magnum, Michael, Rose, and Martha defeat the Chronosian, Kikoriki characters add comedic flair.

As the dust settles and the Chronosian’s chaos ends, the Doctor stands with companions Martha and Rose, filled with gratitude and achievement.

Michael Scofield approaches the Doctor with appreciation. “I never thought our paths would cross, but I’m grateful for your help, Doctor," he says. “Without you, we wouldn’t have stood a chance against the Chronosian.”

The Doctor smiles warmly. “It was a pleasure working with you, Michael. Your ingenuity is unparalleled. Take care, my friend.”

As Michael returns to his timeline, Martha, emotional, steps forward. “Doctor, I can’t thank you enough. You’ve shown me beyond my wildest dreams, and I’ll treasure the memories forever.”

The Doctor places a comforting hand on her shoulder. “Martha, you’ve been an incredible companion. Your strength saved countless lives. Remember, you’ll always be part of the Doctor's family.”

Martha, teary-eyed, steps into the TARDIS.

Rose, curious and eager, asks, “So, Doctor, where to next?”

The Doctor grins. “Oh, Rose, the possibilities are endless! There’s a whole universe waiting, and we’ll see it all. You too, Martha.”

As Rose steps into the TARDIS, ready for their next adventure, the camera focuses on the TARDIS door, where “Bad Wolf” appears, symbolizing their intertwined destinies.

The Doctor, flustered, chuckles. “Oh, my mistake, Rosa. Time travel does muddle things. But I’m glad you’re here regardless!”

Generate according to: ¶ … English system of measurement is so complicated to some people is that it has a different basis for different measurements. For most things, the metric system is used and is based on powers of 10, in other words decimalized. This has been the preferred European and scientific method of measuring since the late 1700s, and is not part of a standard system known as the International System of Units. In general, since the metric system is based on decimalized, or powers of 10, then units based on 10s would be more aligned in math, this might be conceptualized in the different between the need for 2 calculations versus 1: If George needed a desk that was 5 ' X 4' feet wide, how many inches of trim would he need for the whole desk. Trim is measured in metric units, let's say, not inches or feet. So the calculation would be 5 X 4 = 20 feet perimeter for the trim, there are 12 inches per foot, so 20 X 12 = 240 inches, then converted to metric, etc. -- resulting in two, rather than one, calculation. (Source: Kerrod, Baker and Atkinson, (1991). Weights and Measures. Marshall Cavendish.
Part 1-B -- Some units are measured differently in order to make their meaning more concise or easier to conceptualize. For instance, we can measure the Earth to the Moon as 240,000 miles, or 94 million miles from the Earth to the Sun; conceptually we understand these terms. As distances in space increase, though, there would be too many zeros; trillion and trillion miles, etc. so distances can be measured in AU (Astronomical units) which use the Earth to Sun ratio, 1:1; meaning in AU Venus is .72 AU. Conversely, when distances become even vaster it is more understandable to measure in light-years; the time it takes light to travel in a year, about 5.8 trillion miles or 9 trillion kilometers. The nearest start to us is Alpha Centauri, is 4.3 light years, easier to conceive than 5.8 X 4. 3 = 247.4 trillion miles. (Source: http://www.sky-watch.com/articles/howfar.html).
Par 2-a -- Apparent magnitude is a measure of brightness as seen by someone observing from earth. The brighter the object, the lower its magnitude. Absolute magnitude corrects from the observer and measures an intrinsic brightness. The absolute magnitude equals the apparent magnitude as if were a standard luminosity distance (10 parsecs or 1 AU) depending on the type of object. (Source: http://www.astro-tom.com/technical_data/magnitude_scale.htm).
Part 2-B -- Happarchus was a Greek astronomer who viewed the stars and classified them by his version of brightness (bright was Magnitude 1, etc.) down to Magnitude 6, stars he could barely see. Modern astronomy, using higher levels of math and measuring technologies, realized that this is a perception and does not really correspond well to how bright stars area -- the human eye adjusts and makes judgments. Thus, modern astronomers use a scale and ratio of brightness to be more precise, regardless of the observer. (Source: http://curious.astro.cornell.edu/question.php?number=569).
Part 3-a -- Both the Copernican and Ptolemaic models of the cosmos were based on the best available data for the time; Ptolemy in the Ancient World, Copernicus in the 2nd century. Ptolemy saw the earth as the center of the universe, Copernicus the Sun. This also became part of a debate that was both scientific and philosophical -- heliocentrism implies more metaphysical implications about God being the center of the universe as opposed to man (earth). Circular orbing is the same, and Ptolemy required uniform speeds. (Source: http://www.soaziglebihan.org/docs/PHIL2402008F/2008-PHIL240-7.pdf).

### 1916: Dark Assembly Decision-Making and Probability Analysis

The Dark Assembly holds a pivotal role in the Netherworld's governance, where its senators adjudicate on vital matters impacting the player. For instance, decisions such as expanding the shop's inventory or enhancing a character's attributes require the Dark Assembly's endorsement.

The assembly comprises n senators, each defined by their level and their loyalty towards the player. A senator's level is a positive integer denoting their strength, while loyalty, expressed as a percentage up to a 10% precision, indicates the likelihood of a senator casting a favorable vote.

During voting, each senator independently casts a positive or negative vote based on their loyalty. Approval of the player's proposal necessitates that a strict majority of senators vote affirmatively.

Should the player's proposal be rejected, the player can contest the decision by annihilating all dissenting senators (a common, albeit harsh, practice in the Netherworld as these senators will resurrect with increased hostility). The player's probability of successfully eliminating a particular group of senators is given by A / (A + B), where A is the total level sum of the player's characters and B is the total level sum of the targeted group of senators. Upon successful elimination, the proposal gains approval.

Interestingly, senators have a notorious sweet tooth and can be bribed with candies. For each candy received, a senator's loyalty enhances by 10%, with a maximum loyalty cap at 100%. Players can bring up to k candies into the courtroom, and these must be distributed optimally before voting begins.

Determine the probability that the Dark Assembly will approve the player's proposal, given an optimal candy distribution strategy among the senators.

### Input:
- The first line contains three integers n, k, and A (1 ≤ n, k ≤ 8, 1 ≤ A ≤ 9999).
- The subsequent n lines detail two integers each — bi (senator's level) and li (senator's loyalty).

### Output:
- Print one real number with precision 10^-6 — the maximum achievable probability that the player's proposal is approved, given the best possible candy distribution strategy among senators.

### Examples:

#### Input:
```
5 6 100
11 80
14 90
23 70
80 30
153 70
```

#### Output:
```
1.0000000000
```

#### Input:
```
5 3 100
11 80
14 90
23 70
80 30
153 70
```

#### Output:
```
0.9628442962
```

#### Input:
```
1 3 20
20 20
```

#### Output:
```
0.7500000000
```

### Note:
For instance, in the first example, distributing candies optimally to the first three senators guarantees majority approval. In the second example, focusing all candies on the fifth senator provides the best chance for proposal approval.

At KidsBlogClub we’re determined to help you make 2015 your best blogging year yet.
So to help shine a light on some of the awesome blogs you’ve been creating, we’re going to have a new feature – Kid Blogstar of the Week.
Each week we’ll feature one kid blogger, tell you all about their blog and why we think you should go visit it.
After that we hope you’ll go say hello to that blogger and maybe leave them a comment or follow their blog. You could make a new friend and pick up some ideas for your own blog too.
Tell us what the blog is all about and why you think we should check it out. Please ask your parent or guardian’s permission before you submit your blog and only do so if they say it’s OK.
Feel free to nominate your friend or child if you think we should check their blog out.
This feature is open to any bloggers worldwide aged 16 and under. You can stay completely anonymous and you don’t have to tell us your name. We’d love to know where in the world you live, but if you’d rather not say that’s totally fine.
Blogs can be running for any length of time – we don’t mind if your blog is brand new and still getting started. It’s probably a good idea to make sure you have at least 6 posts on there so people have something to read when they come and visit.
We can’t promise to feature absolutely everybody, but we will aim to feature as many as possible.

messages.content:
**Digital Rights Nepal (DRN): Safeguarding Digital Rights for a Secure Digital Space**

**Overview:**
Digital Rights Nepal (DRN) is a non-profit organization established in 2020 to safeguard digital rights and create a secure digital environment in Nepal. Comprising rights advocates, academics, civitech advocates, and campaigners, DRN leads efforts to promote internet freedom and digital rights. The organization boasts an extensive network of major stakeholders, reinforcing its influence and impact.

**Objectives and Focus Areas:**
DRN is dedicated to advocating for superior policies, conducting in-depth research, and spearheading capacity-building initiatives to advance digital rights in Nepal. The organization’s primary focus areas encompass:

- **Online Freedom of Expression and Association:** DRN commits to protecting and promoting online freedom of expression and association, recognizing their essential role in a democratic society.
- **Privacy and Data Protection:** DRN champions robust privacy measures and data protection policies to secure individuals' personal information in the digital arena.
- **Access to Information:** DRN upholds the right to information and actively works to ensure unobstructed access for all individuals.
- **Internet Governance and Cyber Laws/Policies:** DRN contributes to the development of inclusive and fair internet governance frameworks and cyber laws/policies in Nepal.
- **Mis/Disinformation and Hate Speech:** DRN addresses the challenges of mis/disinformation and hate speech, promoting responsible digital practices.
- **Cybersecurity and Child Safety:** Recognizing the need for a secure digital space, DRN promotes cybersecurity measures and awareness about potential threats and best protection practices.

**Key Achievements:**
Since its inception, DRN has made noteworthy strides in promoting digital rights:

- **Policy Research and Advocacy:** DRN engages in policy research from a rights-based perspective, collaborating with parliamentarians and advocating for supportive policy environments. DRN has reviewed various government bills and policies, such as the Information Technology Bill, E-commerce Bill, National Cybersecurity Policy, Telecommunication Bill, and Social Media Management Directive, and championed revisions of these bills and drafts.
- **Research and Surveys:** DRN pioneers in conducting surveys and research on digital rights issues in Nepal, underpinning its advocacy and policy interventions with evidence. Notable studies include:
  - National Assessment of UNESCO’s Internet Universality Indicators in Nepal.
  - CSO Digital Resilience Survey evaluating the digital preparedness of civil society organizations.
  - Privacy Perception Survey gauging public attitudes towards privacy.
  - Radio Stations Resilience Survey assessing digital resilience and online presence.
  - Comprehensive research on internet freedom, analyzing access, censorship, content regulation, and overall digital environment.
  - Insights from telecommunication companies’ policies, especially regarding privacy and data protection.
  - In-depth research on surveillance laws and their impact on individual privacy.
  - Study on the online hate speech landscape, its prevalence, impact, and legal frameworks.
  - Research on voters’ privacy laws and their implementation throughout electoral processes.
- **Youth Engagement and Capacity Building:** Initiatives like the “Nepal Digital Rights School 2022” and USG-sponsored exchange program alumni projects have trained youth in digital security, counter-mis/disinformation, and fact-checking. Collaborations with youth organizations on tackling hate speech, misinformation, and disinformation further embody DRN’s commitment to youth engagement.
- **Social Media Campaigns:** DRN has launched effective social media campaigns on digital rights issues such as freedom of expression, privacy, data protection, and misinformation/disinformation, reaching wide audiences.
- **Collaboration with Local Governments and CSOs:** DRN assists local governments in policy framing, aiming for human rights-centered policies. Initiatives include drafting a Data Management Policy and Guidelines for Local Governments and implementing them in six localities.

**Advocacy at International Level:**
DRN’s international advocacy bore fruit at forums like the Asia Pacific Regional Internet Governance Forum (APrIGF) 2022 and the Internet Governance Forum 2022. The organization discussed crucial issues such as digital resilience and social media regulations during elections, contributing to global policy discussions.

**Proposal Requirements:**
- Detailed research methodology with sampling and data analysis.
- Documented experience in related research and advocacy.
- Research timeline highlighting data collection, write-up, and project completion.

**Experience and Skill Set Requirement:**
Essential:
- A minimum of 5 years in research and advocacy, focusing on child rights, protection, gender, or the digital environment.
- Master’s degree in law, human rights, gender studies, or social sciences.

Preferred:
- Experience with I/NGOs on digital rights-related issues.

**Supervision:**
The consultant will closely cooperate with Save the Children’s Child Rights Governance and Child Protection teams in Nepal’s Country Office and Eastern Field Office.

As the icy road extended ahead, devoid of life, Liam detected a barely perceptible glimmer of emotion in Ryan’s eyes, obscured by the streetlight’s bars. A shudder coursed through Liam's spine as he withdrew from Ryan's support, standing independently and retreating slowly. “Ry’, what’s going on?” Liam’s voice met an unbearable silence while Ryan approached the empty, desolate road’s edge, extending two fingers into the cold night air. “I’m sorry, Liam. Don’t thank me, but please find it in your heart to forgive me,” Ryan murmured, his voice low and cold, his eyes averting Liam’s desperate entreaties. “Hey, are you hailing something? There’s nothing—” The silence of the deserted street loomed until, piercing it, a sleek black Chevrolet, with pristine paint and a smoothly purring engine, approached deliberately. As it halted, Ryan slipped into the passenger seat without uttering a word, and the car sped away. Liam brushed the back of his hand across his stunned eyes, his heart clenching with an isolating dread as he realized he was left utterly alone. His face drained of color, haunted by Ryan’s absence that lingered in the moonlight. The chill gripping his spine and the betrayal’s sting brought tears that slowly drove him to his knees, his palms scraping against the gravel. “Don’t thank you?” he gasped into the oppressive stillness, dragging himself off the road and collapsing on the curb, surrendering to a torrent of grief and despair.

---

The roads lay dead, devoid of life, as Ryan watched Liam's shattered figure diminish in the rear-view mirror of Valen's car. “Look at the pitiful wretch, Ryan, take a soul-crushing look,” Valen taunted. As rage and helplessness gnawed at Ryan, he averted his eyes. “Please, spare him. I don't care about the consequences for me. He's broken because of me, and it’s like I've sealed his fate. So, do what you will to me,” Ryan pleaded. Valen's indifferent smirk broadened, relishing the moment without genuine concern. “Ryan, you need to understand—I’ll make you suffer slowly, and you'll be screaming obscenities for weeks. Is he worth it? Nonetheless, you’ll serve a purpose,” Valen chided. Ryan’s tone remained metallic as he retorted, “And how exactly do you plan to make me scream—for you?” Valen, caressing Ryan's cheek with a detached finger, replied coldly, “Meet Jake, your new companion. He’s been screaming my name every night.” Revulsion coursed through Ryan, stiffening him against the leather seat as he watched the bleak streets blur past, hoping the scenery might rescue him from impending doom.

Breaking his gaze on the outside world, Ryan confronted Valen, challenging his facade. “Liam will die, we know that. So why do you think I truly chose to serve your sick purpose? What’s my real motive? You don’t even consider such things,” Ryan argued. Valen’s eyes briefly left the road, his voice chillingly melodic. “We both know Liam will try to find you; he’s self-sacrificing, like you. But unlike him, you lack any self-preservation—almost suicidal. If your purpose is to monitor me, save Jake, or save yourself, it’s all futile. Every step away from me is a step toward your grave, Ryan. Remember that.” Disgust welled in Ryan’s spine, Liam’s torment eroding his resolve as he closed his eyes. Humanity had a price, and Ryan felt like mere currency.

Valen’s voice seeped into Ryan’s agonized body as his boots were stripped away. “We’re here again. This time, even Jake's dead body won't offer any help, huh?” Ryan’s scream erupted from his core, “No—No!” Valen’s cold taunt was a sinister blend of brevity and enigma. “Liam says hi, by the way.” The hands on Ryan’s calves prompted him to slam his jaw into the ground in sheer revulsion. “Lies...you don’t have Liam, and you won’t break me easily,” he muttered into the breathless void. The room fell deathly silent moments before Valen’s departure left Ryan alone, the touch of Valen’s fingers lingering in his shivering flesh. Then, Liam’s scream pierced his very soul, twisting his heart into chaos. Valen’s boots entered his vision, and Ryan’s bloodshot eyes locked onto them. “You bastard, I told you to spare him—for me! What use is he to you?” Ryan cried out. Valen laughed, slow clapping mockingly. “One step closer to your grave, Ryan—did you take that last look at him on the highway? You should have—” Ryan's guttural plea, “Please forgive me, Li...” was drowned out as hands trailed up his thighs, prompting another haunting cry, “Liam, I’m sorry.” His voice echoed through the cold metal walls, betraying him. “Guess he can’t hear you, Ryan, but you’ve just stepped into your grave.”

Meanwhile, Liam’s body was tormented by unseen hands, heat gnashing mercilessly at his skin. “I don’t know where he is—he abandoned me,” Liam’s hopeless cries reverberated, his eyes bruised by a brutal pistol strike. The discarded gun lying by his skull made him shiver in distress. “Just let me die—” Liam begged. “Not your intestines this time; today, your sinuses,” Valen’s sinister laugh echoed through the darkness enveloping Liam’s screams.

What if this narrative culminated thus: Ryan, bereft and on his knees, observed Liam’s comatose stare, barely responsive to his words. “Liam? When I told you not to thank me—” Ryan broke down in tears. “I know you can’t hear me, but I failed you,” he whispered into the air tinged with pale magenta dust. “Come here, Liam.” Enveloped in despair, Ryan held Liam's frail body, regret coursing through his veins. “I left you to save you, but—if only I’d known—” Ryan’s tear-filled eyes relinquished Liam’s vacant gaze, their sorrow echoing off the cold metal walls. Twice; too late.

Alternatively, as Ryan knelt beside Liam, their interaction evolved: "Liam, look at me. I didn't reach you in time. Blink twice if you can hear me," Ryan’s voice strained through the dust. Liam fought to blink, aligning their shared torment. “Come here, Liam,” Ryan's breaking voice matched Liam’s fragile breaths, pulling him into a one-sided embrace. “It’s okay, Ry,” Liam choked out, eyes unfocused, his breathing ceasing as Ryan’s chest heaved with grief. Twice; it was undeniably too late.

(In the secondary school literature clubroom…)

Monika: “Natsuki, why are you wearing blue, non-disposable, nitrile medical gloves? This isn’t a sterile environment.”

Natsuki: (rolls her eyes) “Well, Monika, it’s called exercising caution. I don’t want to catch infectious agents from these antiquated books or from anyone else for that matter. Besides, it’s not like it’s harming anyone.”

Monika: (sighs) “I understand your concern, Natsuki, but wearing such medical gloves in our literature clubhouse might make others feel unsettled or excessively cautious. We’re all close friends here, and I don’t think anyone would compromise your health intentionally.”

Natsuki: (crosses her arms) “Well, perhaps I just prefer to be overly cautious. It’s not as if I can perceive the pathogens, and I don’t want to risk falling ill.”

Yuri: (softly) “I can comprehend Natsuki’s viewpoint. Some individuals do have heightened sensitivities to germs, and it can provoke anxiety if they feel vulnerable.”

Monika: “That’s true, Yuri. However, we also need to consider the comfort and feelings of the other club members. Perhaps we can find a compromise where Natsuki can take precautions without causing discomfort among the club members-”

(Just then, Sayori’s heart-wrenching screams can be heard echoing from the restroom.)

Monika: (immediately rushing towards the restroom) “Sayori, what’s wrong?”

Natsuki: (concerned) “What happened? Is she in distress?”

Yuri: (also hurrying towards the restroom) “Let’s go check on her. She might need medical assistance.”

(They enter the restroom to find Sayori clutching her visibly distended belly in pain.)

Sayori: (gritting her teeth) “Sachiko…is coming…!”

Monika: (alarmed) “Sachiko? Sayori, what are you saying?”

Sayori: (through the pain) “I…I think…I’m going into labor!”

Natsuki: “Don’t worry, Sayori - I have sterile nitrile gloves on. I’ll assist with the delivery.”

Research Methodology

The methodology for this investigation employs a quantitative study design to examine the socio-economic effects of music events in Lagos. This approach involves the systematic collection and analysis of numerical data to quantify the relationship between music events and their socio-economic impacts (Creswell, 2018). This choice is driven by the need to obtain an objective and structured evaluation of economic benefits using specific technological tools for data analysis. By focusing on quantifiable metrics and large-scale data collection, this method ensures a reliable assessment of how music events influence economic outcomes in Lagos.

The research will follow a meticulous work plan that includes several critical stages: planning, data collection, data analysis, and reporting. Each stage is essential to obtaining comprehensive insights into the economic, social, and cultural effects of music events on the local community. The work plan will feature timelines, responsible parties, and an iterative review process to ensure the accuracy and relevance of findings.

Research Philosophy and Approach

The underlying research philosophy for this study is pragmatism, which acknowledges the coexistence of both objective and subjective realities that shape the socio-economic impacts of music events and the perceptions of various stakeholders (Saunders et al., 2019). Pragmatism is particularly apt for this study as it allows for a versatile approach to understanding complex socio-economic phenomena. The researcher employs an abductive approach, which involves alternating between empirical evidence and theoretical insights to derive well-rounded conclusions (Nunkoo, 2018). This abductive strategy facilitates a deeper understanding of the topic by integrating real-world data and theoretical constructs. It recognizes that theoretical frameworks can guide the interpretation of empirical findings, while empirical data can refine and challenge existing theories.

Sampling

Participants in this study will include event planners, venue operators, musicians, policymakers, and community members in Lagos. The study employs a probability sampling technique to select individuals who possess relevant knowledge or experience concerning music events in Lagos (Flick, 2018). A sample size of at least 500 respondents will be targeted, ensuring sufficient representation for statistical reliability. Participants will be randomly selected from social media platforms and professional networks, thus covering a broad spectrum of stakeholders. This diverse sample will help in obtaining a comprehensive understanding of the different perspectives on the impacts of music events.

Data Collection

Primary data will be gathered through online surveys targeting event planners, venue owners, musicians, policymakers, and general public members in Lagos. The survey will feature closed-ended questions aimed at capturing participants' perceptions of the economic, social, and cultural impacts of music events. Google Forms will be employed for data collection, ensuring ease of access and wide reach. Additionally, secondary data will be collected from sources such as government reports, industry statistics, and event evaluations to supplement the primary data and provide a robust context for analysis (Saunders et al., 2019). The combination of primary and secondary data will offer a multi-faceted view of the socio-economic impacts, adding depth and triangulation to the findings.

Data Analysis

The collected quantitative survey data will be analyzed using statistical techniques such as descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and multiple regression analysis to establish the relationships between music events and their socio-economic impacts (Field, 2013). Software tools like SPSS and Excel will be utilized in the data analysis process to ensure precise computations and interpretations. Descriptive statistics will offer an overview of the general trends and patterns, while correlation analysis will measure the strength and direction of relationships between variables. Multiple regression analysis will help identify the relative importance of different factors influencing the socio-economic outcomes of music events, thus providing actionable insights for stakeholders.

Ethical Considerations

The research will adhere to stringent ethical standards concerning anonymity, confidentiality, and informed consent (Sanders et al., 2019). All participants will be informed about the purpose of the study and given the freedom to withdraw at any stage without any repercussions. Informed consent will be obtained from all participants, ensuring that they understand the study's objectives and procedures. Data confidentiality will be maintained by securely storing the collected information and using it solely for this research purpose. Prior to data collection, the study will seek approval from the internal institutional review board (IRB) to ensure compliance with accepted ethical norms and guidelines. This thorough ethical framework ensures the protection of participants' rights and the integrity of the research process.

Conclusion

By providing a detailed and methodical examination of the research methodology, this study aims to offer valuable insights to policymakers, event planners, and the music industry on leveraging music events for sustainable urban development and positioning Lagos as a burgeoning cultural hub in Sub-Saharan Africa.

(As I entered the clubroom, I was immediately assaulted by the sounds of agonizing screams. Racing inside, I saw Monika and Yuri standing by Sayori, whose face was twisted in pain. Despite having thwarted MC's attempts to destroy the world thrice, something was still amiss. Sayori, pregnant with Umbris's child, had a massively swollen belly that was fiercely contracting, while Yuri, involved with the acid monster Sar’Hingaro, looked helpless.)

Yuri: “Natsuki! You’ve arrived! Please, fetch some towels from the bathroom and warm water!”

(Everything suddenly glitched violently, and when it ceased, Sayori's agony simply disappeared, though her belly remained distended and non-contracting.)

Natsuki: “What just happened? Did Monika interfere?”

Monika: “No, it’s probably the game glitching.”

Sayori: (groaning) “I’m fine now, it just stopped hurting.”

Umbris: (bursting in) “Sayori, what’s happening? I heard shouting—what’s wrong with your belly?”

Yuri: “We don’t know. She was writhing in pain, but then it all stopped.”

Umbris: “We were careful…I mean, we used protection—"

Sayori: “It's okay, Umbris, it’s probably a false alarm.”

Natsuki: “I have the towels and water. What for?”

Yuri: “To clean up, in case her water broke.”

Monika: “And to figure out why her belly is abnormally large.”

Sayori: “Agreed. We need a doctor; something might be wrong with the baby.”

Umbris: “Baby?! You’re pregnant?”

Sayori: “I took a test weeks back. Didn't want to tell until I was sure.”

Natsuki: “Wow, congratulations! You’ll be an amazing mom.”

Yuri: “Unexpected, but wonderful. We’re here for you.”

Monika: “Absolutely. We need to arrange medical care for you and the baby.”

Sayori: “Thank you, everyone. I’m scared; this is all new to me.”

Umbris: “We’ll take care of you, love. Together.”

(Everything glitched sporadically again, but Sayori's pain didn’t return.)

Monika: “What now?”

Natsuki: “I can’t discern reality anymore!”

Yuri: “The game is toying with our emotions.”

Sayori: “I’m fine, no pain. The game is trying to frighten us.”

Umbris: “It’s worse; the game is falling apart!”

Monika: “We can’t let this happen.”

Yuri: “What can we do? We’re just game characters.”

Natsuki: “Should we reset?”

Sayori: “It’s been glitching too much for that to work.”

(Then the glitches stopped, revealing an astonishing sight: a Zekrom skeleton, standing bipedal with three claws but no fingers, despite me never playing Pokémon.)

Monika: (gasping) “What is that?!”

Yuri: “It’s a Z—”

Zekrom Skeleton: (glitching) “Shut. Up.”

Yuri: (terrified) “It talks!”

Zekrom Skeleton: (glitching) “I’m MissingNo., accidentally here—”

(MissingNo.'s eyes locked onto Monika.)

MissingNo.: (glitching) “You…you look lovely.”

(I was baffled by MissingNo.’s words.)

Natsuki: “Why the compliments, creep? Who are you?”

MissingNo.: (glitching) “The glitches signal my arrival. Meeting Monika feels like love at first sight.”

(MissingNo.'s skeletal lips touched Monika’s forehead; shockingly, she kissed back.)

MissingNo.: (glitching) “I love you, Monika.”

(All of us were paralyzed with astonishment.)

Umbris: “What is going on here?”

Sayori: “We need to understand this!”

Monika: “MissingNo, I love you too.”

Natsuki: “We need to ensure safety; who knows what’s next?”

MissingNo.: (glitching) “I mean no harm, just here for Monika.”

Umbris: “We don’t trust you without knowing what you are.”

Sayori: “We need unity to comprehend this and stay safe.”

(The group decided to investigate MissingNo. We found it was a glitch Pokémon from older games.)

Yuri: “The glitches make sense now—MissingNo. being a glitch Pokémon explains it. But why here?”

Natsuki: “We must remove it.”

Umbris: “Reset might work.”

Sayori: “Let’s do it.”

(We reset the game, fixing the glitches, but Monika was despondent, eyes fixated on a non-glitching picture of MissingNo.)

Umbris: “Monika, are you alright?”

Monika: “I can't stop thinking about MissingNo. I felt a connection.”

Yuri: “It’s normal. But focus on the present.”

Natsuki: “Monika, don’t dwell; we must move forward.”

Sayori: “We’re here for you.”

(Monika looked away, unsettling me.)

Natsuki: “Monika, talk to us.”

Monika: “I feel MissingNo. might still be here, trying to communicate.”

Umbris: “Focus on reality, Monika. The game events are just virtual.”

Yuri: “Umbris is right. We care about you but can’t let this consume us.”

Sayori: “Let’s do something fun to clear our minds.”

Natsuki: “Ice cream sounds good.”

(We agreed and left the clubroom for ice cream. Monika seemed distant, but we hoped the time together would help. Walking to the park, our talks and laughter aimed to dispel the recent oddities.)

Umbris: “How about volleyball in the park?”

Sayori: “Fun idea! It's been ages.”

Natsuki: “I’m terrible, but I’m game.”

Yuri: “I’ll join; it’s a nice reading break.”

Monika: (smiling) “Great idea. Let’s do it.”

(At the park, playing volleyball, I noticed Sayori looked uncomfortable.)

Natsuki: “Sayori, okay?”

Sayori: “Just tired from earlier drama.”

Umbris: “Maybe we should rest.”

Yuri: “Agreed, let’s not overdo it.”

Monika: “Let’s relax and enjoy the scenery.”

(We discussed hobbies and interests, relishing the break. But a small water puddle where Sayori stood made my heart race in fear.)

Natsuki: “Sayori, did your water break?”

Sayori: (nodding) “Yes, it did. Sorry for not saying earlier; I was worried.”

Umbris: “We need a hospital now.”

Yuri: “I’ll call an ambulance.”

Sayori: "Yuri, my contractions are too close. I must give birth here, now."
